narration_transcript.title: The problem
narration_transcript.text: A PayPal dispute is decided on evidence: a tracking number, a delivery confirmation, a message thread. By day forty-one, the tracking number was never attached to the PayPal order, and the buyer is already saying chargeback. Merchants lose these cases on paperwork they no longer have.

narration_transcript.title: What it is
narration_transcript.text: MerchantShield AI scores every order, proposes the action that saves the evidence, and executes only after a human approves. Every record carries one of three labels: a real Sandbox response, generated locally, or a mock standing in for PayPal. There is no fourth label.

narration_transcript.title: Scoring an order
narration_transcript.text: Twenty-five hand-written rules score each order from zero to one, and every point is attributed with a direction. No tracking costs twenty points. You can argue with a rule; you cannot argue with a number that appears from nowhere.

narration_transcript.title: Estimate and evidence
narration_transcript.text: Beside it, a logistic-regression prototype, clearly labelled estimate, trained on synthetic data, with its metrics and two baselines on the Methodology page. Underneath, the seven documents this kind of case needs, which ones you hold, and what to do about each gap.

narration_transcript.title: Acting on it, safely
narration_transcript.text: Ask the planner, and it proposes actions: attach this tracking number, message the buyer, flag the order. Everything arrives pending. The agent has no write access. Approve, then execute. The claim is a single conditional update, so two clicks cannot create two tracking numbers.

narration_transcript.title: Once, and honestly unknown
narration_transcript.text: A test fires eight concurrent executes and asserts exactly one claim, one external call and one audit row. And a timeout is not a failure. It is an unknown, and the app refuses a blind retry, because that is how duplicates happen.

narration_transcript.title: The dispute
narration_transcript.text: When the case does open, the packet is already assembled. The draft is a deterministic template without a key; with a Gemini key it is a model draft that must pass a hallucination guard. Every save is a new version. Submission is labelled simulated: no case is filed with PayPal.

narration_transcript.title: Why you can trust it
narration_transcript.text: Every state change is in an append-only audit log, with an actor and a source. The Methodology page prints the model's real numbers next to two baselines, and states what is not built: no production PayPal, no dispute filing, no carrier API, no training on PayPal data.

narration_transcript.title: What it changes
narration_transcript.text: For a small merchant, that is the difference between arguing a case and losing it by default. Evidence collected on day one is worth more than any percentage a dashboard could invent. And when the app does not know something, it says so.

narration_transcript.title: Where it stands
narration_transcript.text: Two hundred and fifteen backend tests, thirty-two browser tests and sixteen mutation checks run from one command. If a guarantee is removed, a test fails. PayPal Sandbox only. Nothing here moves real money.
